name: Lole
confidence_why: 3 independent first-hand descriptions agree (2 state the same rule, 0 refine it); none contradicts.

audit.action: a better source should be cited for the same classification
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: the deciding quotation from Edwards 2021 sec. 2.4.1 is verbatim on pp.35-36 of the PDF we hold/text (held by the project, not under lole1239, which is why the record shows we have no copy). (2) Deciding source: a 2021 open-access comparative dictionary (ANU Press) whose background chapter states stress for 'the Rote languages' as a group; for Lole this is second-hand/family-level (Lole data there come from an unpublished 2014 UBB Toolbox lexicon). Glottolog 5.1 has zero descriptive references for lole1239. Web search (ILCAA/TUFS, Linguistik Indonesia, ResearchGate, SIL/UBB, LingDy) found one Lole-specific sketch: Balukh, Shiohara & Thine 2023 (AALL 17:127-149), downloaded now; p.131 says stress 'usually occurs penultimately' and falls on the first vowel of a (heterosyllabic) vowel sequence, with examples [ˈbu.sa], [ka.li.ˈkɛ.ɛ], [ʔa.ka.ˈnda.a] —

sources.citation: Edwards 2021, Rote-Meto Comparative Dictionary, ANU Press, sec. 2.4.1, full PDF via OAPEN (handle 20.500.12657/52033)
sources.quote: Stress falls on the penultimate vowel of a word with secondary stress assigned to every second syllable to the left. ... Given the placement of stress, one member of a vowel sequence will always bear stress.

sources.citation: Balukh, Jermy I., Asako Shiohara & Elsijon M. Thine. 2023. The Legend of Inggu Fufuk, or the Beetle Village: A Folktale of Lole, a Language Spoken on Rote Island. Asian and African Languages and Linguistics 17: 127-149. ILCAA, TUFS.
sources.quote: 'vowel sequences in Lole form two separate syllables instead of long vowels or diphthongs constituting one syllable. ... Second, the stress, which usually occurs penultimately (e.g., [ˈbu.sa] ‘dog’ and [ˈpɛ.kɔk] ‘bent’, ...), occurs on the first vowel of the sequence (e.g., [ˈda.ɛ] ‘ground’, [ˈbɔ.ɔk] ‘smell’, [ka.li.ˈkɛ.ɛ] ‘belt’, and [ʔa.ka.ˈnda.a] ‘1sg-doubt’).' Also sec. 2.4: syllable template (C)V(C), codas only /k s n/, root-final only.
sources.note: Only Lole-specific grammatical sketch in print; states penultimate stress for Lole with IPA examples (p.131), whereas our deciding quote is a pan-Rote sentence in a comparative dictionary. Should become the primary citation.
sources.venue: Asian and African Languages and Linguistics

sources.citation: Tamelan, Thersia M., Dendi Wijaya, Festif R. Hoinbala & I Gusti Ayu Gde Sosiowati. 2026. Orthographic Transparency of Rote Speech Varieties: Challenges in Language Learning. Linguistik Indonesia 44(2): 287-306. doi:10.26499/li.v44i2.1071
sources.quote: Rote-wide: 'Monosyllabic words act as functors and do not carry stress, whereas disyllabic words are lexical and carry penultimate stress. ... the stress is placed on the penultimate vowel. This is the first vowel for disyllabic words, while for trisyllabic words, it is the second vowel.' Examples are Dela; Lole appears only in the orthography tables (tehuu, tolanoo etc.). No Lole-specific stress sentence.
sources.locator: pp.298-300 (double vowels), Table 9 includes Lole (UBB) forms

tone.quote: Tekanan Kata Dalam bahasa Lole tekanan kata jatuh pada vokal kedua dari belakang di kata dasar (akar kata). [Di bawah ini: K = konsonan; V = vokal]. ... Jika vokal panjang tidak ditulis, maka bahasa Lole tidak bisa dibaca dalam kalimat dengan lagu dan tekanan yang sebenarnya. ... Oleh karena tekanan kata jatuh pada vokal kedua dari belakang, maka beberapa kata penghubung sebenarnya merupakan frase, sehingga perlu ditulis secara terpisah, bukan secara bergabung. ... Akhiran kata benda yang berbentuk suku kata (yang kebetulan enclitic) tidak mengambil tekanan kata.
tone.locator: section 'Tekanan Kata', pp. 3-4 (footer 'Sistem Penulisan Bahasa Lole - 3/4')
tone.translation: Word stress. In the Lole language word stress falls on the second vowel from the end in the base word (root). [Below: K = consonant; V = vowel]. ... If long vowels are not written, Lole cannot be read in sentences with the true melody and stress. ... Because word stress falls on the second vowel from the end, some connectives are actually phrases and must be written separately, not joined. ... Noun suffixes that form a syllable (which happen to be enclitic) do not take word stress.
